body: What do the &variables do and why did you remove these?
This is super odd syntax! What does it do? `?;`

`&variables` are references to an object, rather than objects themselves.
It's good practice to use instances where possible as it's lighter in memory to pass a reference around than an instance.

https://github.com/starship/starship/pull/6/files/daeb7cf6bfbd170f149ea98a73bfa5d5a5b67a07#diff-95036686adb679a23cd72cd4cca8cbc9R17
In this case (`current_dir: &Path`) `current_dir` is a reference to a `Path`, so I don't need to add the ampersand. If instead, the function param accepted `current_dir: Path`, I would refer to it with `&current_dir` so that I was using the reference.

More details here: https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-02-references-and-borrowing.html#references-and-borrowing

`let temp_dir = TempDir::new("starship")?;` will compile into:
```rust
match TempDir::new("starship") {
    Ok(dir)  => dir,
    Err(err) => return Err(err),
}
```

It's a quick way to return an `Error` if the function around it is a `Result` (which will allow returning `Error`s).

More details here: https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2018/error-handling-and-panics/the-question-mark-operator-for-easier-error-handling.html
